lines.text: A seven-billion-parameter model runs on a laptop in fourteen gigabytes.
Training the same model needs a hundred and twelve.
That gap is arithmetic. It is worth doing carefully, because every term in it is a decision somebody made.
Start with the weights. Seven billion parameters at sixteen bits each is fourteen gigabytes.
Training also needs the gradients. Another fourteen gigabytes.
Then the optimizer. Adam keeps two running averages per parameter, momentum and variance, in full precision.
That is eight bytes per parameter. Two more copies of the model, held as state.
Fourteen, plus fourteen, plus fifty-six. Eighty-four gigabytes before a single activation.
Activations scale with batch size and sequence length, not with model size.
So the honest total depends on your configuration. At batch one and sequence four thousand, it lands near a hundred and twelve gigabytes.
You can make it fit. Shard it across eight GPUs, and each one holds an eighth.
But sharding does not delete the memory. It splits it, and adds the cost of the GPUs talking to each other.
A model you cannot fit is a model you cannot run. That is why training costs what it costs.
